protocol.pause_model: in-process renewal pause; not a process-kill or storage-durability claim
protocol.workflow_transition: new owner applies WAITING_ACTIVITY transition after takeover

conclusions.recovery: Observed owner-pause takeover medians were 125.3 ms at 100 ms, 276.2 ms at 250 ms, and 776.9 ms at 750 ms; these are expiry-detection measurements, not process-crash recovery times.
conclusions.renewal_traffic: Normal-renewal traffic averaged 170.7, 94.3, and 57.7 renewals per run for 100, 250, and 750 ms TTLs; shorter leases require more renewal traffic in this bounded cohort.
conclusions.safety: Safety control passed: 0 false takeovers, 108 useful recoveries for 108 takeovers, and 324 stale-owner writes rejected.
conclusions.lock_contention: The campaign measured 9 lock-contention cases and 0.1835 cumulative lock-wait seconds; this is local PostgreSQL contention evidence, not a production capacity estimate.
conclusions.pause_interpretation: Owner pauses stop renewal inside the campaign process. They intentionally exercise lease expiry and fencing without claiming equivalence to a hard kill or host failure.

limitations: single-node PostgreSQL on the declared Docker Desktop/WSL2 host
owner pauses are bounded in-process fixtures rather than process termination
results do not establish multi-host, hard-kill, production scheduler, or maximum-throughput behavior
short-TTL arms are measurement configurations, not recommended deployment settings
